Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3448); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite:--Jesse.
BiblicalUsage: Jesse was the father of David, a farmer of Bethlehem whose name carries the whole promise. In Matthew 1:5 Salmon begat Booz of Rachab, and Booz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse, in Romans 15:12 Isaiah's word is quoted, there shall be a root of Jesse, and in Acts 13:22 God says he found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jesse's obscurity is the point: God raised a king from a Bethlehem farmer's house, and the root of Jesse became the hope of the Gentiles.
